column2: Which radio feedline specification should match the antenna input for efficient transfer of radio-frequency power?
column7: The antenna and its feedline should present matching impedances at the operating frequency. A DC resistance measurement does not establish that match.

column2: A VHF tower fades as an airplane descends behind terrain. Which normal propagation mode explains the change?
column7: Normal VHF air-to-ground coverage depends mainly on an unobstructed path between the antennas. Climbing can clear an intervening obstacle.

column2: Which airframe fitting reduces radio noise caused by charge collected while flying through precipitation?
column7: A static wick discharges accumulated charge at points selected to reduce radio interference. Without suitable discharge paths, corona pulses can produce receiver noise.

column2: Why does a 406 MHz emergency locator transmitter also send a low-power 121.5 MHz signal?
column7: The low-power signal helps rescuers home on the beacon near the site. The digital 406 MHz transmission supplies the satellite alert.

column2: An aircraft is directly above a DME station. Why does the displayed distance remain greater than zero?
column3: It measures the direct radio path
column6: It includes distance to the next fix
column7: DME uses the round-trip time of a radio signal to measure slant range. Directly overhead the separation is essentially the height above the station.

column2: On an ILS approach, which signal provides lateral guidance to the runway centerline?
column7: The localizer provides left-right guidance. The glide slope supplies the independent vertical component.

column2: Which airborne function transmits the aircraft's position and ground speed to compatible surveillance receivers?
column7: ADS-B Out broadcasts the aircraft's own surveillance data. ADS-B In lets suitably equipped aircraft receive available traffic and weather information.

column2: An airborne airplane with failed radio receives a steady red tower light. What does the signal direct?
column6: Remain clear because the airport is unsafe
column7: A steady red light to an aircraft in flight requires it to give way and keep circling. Flashing red warns that landing is unsafe.

column2: A mechanic taxiing an airplane receives a flashing white tower signal. What instruction applies?
column7: Flashing white directs an aircraft on the ground back to its starting point on the airport.

column2: Two synchronized flashing lights flank a runway threshold. What are they identifying?
column7: Runway end identifier lights distinguish the approach end from nearby lighting or terrain. The pair flashes together at the sides of the threshold.

column2: A landing airplane passes alternating red and white runway centerline lights. What distance remains in this zone?
column7: Centerline lights alternate during the 2,000 feet before the final 1,000 feet. All centerline lights in that last 1,000 feet are red.

column2: How long is the yellow edge-light caution zone on a 3,200-foot instrument runway?
column7: The yellow segment is the shorter of 2,000 feet and half the runway length. Half of 3,200 feet is 1,600 feet.

column2: Two vented avgas tanks supply one carburetor by gravity. Which measurement determines their relative static fuel heads?
column3: Height of each fuel surface above the inlet
column4: Length of each tank's supply hose
column5: Internal diameter of each outlet tube
column6: Area of each tank's exposed fuel surface
column7: Both tanks contain the same fuel at atmospheric pressure. The difference in static head therefore comes from the height of each fuel surface relative to the common inlet.

column2: Which component can maintain delivery if the engine-driven pump fails in a conventional dual-pump fuel system?
column7: The auxiliary electric pump provides backup delivery to the engine. A transfer pump moves fuel between storage locations.

column2: Where does a conventional hand primer discharge fuel on a carbureted piston helicopter before starting?
column7: The primer has a separate path to the cylinder intake ports. It enriches the starting charge when cold fuel is difficult to vaporize in the carburetor.

column2: A mechanic wants to sample free water after an avgas tank stands undisturbed. Which location is most informative?
column3: Sump at the bottom of the tank
column4: Fuel surface near the filler opening
column5: Pickup just above the unusable fuel level
column6: Mid-depth level at the quantity probe
column7: Water is denser than aviation gasoline and settles below it. Fuel system sumps collect water and sediment at low points.

column2: A drawing shows fuel held by sealed wing skin, ribs, and spars. Which tank construction does it show?
column7: In a wet wing the sealed structure itself forms the fuel container. Separate bladders and rigid tanks carry fuel inside their own walls.

column2: For a 500-gallon transport airplane tank, what minimum expansion space does 14 CFR 25.969 specify?
column7: The minimum expansion space is 2 percent of tank capacity. Two percent of 500 gallons is 10 gallons.

column2: What keeps the pressure in a conventional unpressurized fuel tank near ambient as fuel leaves?
column7: The vent connects the tank airspace with outside air. It admits replacement air as the fuel level falls.

column2: In a fixed-geometry capacitive fuel probe, which property changes as liquid rises between the electrodes?
column5: Total area of the metal plates
column7: Fuel has a higher dielectric constant than air. As fuel occupies more space between the probe electrodes, capacitance increases.

column2: In level flight, when must a transport airplane's fuel quantity indicator be calibrated to zero?
column4: When the tank is completely dry
column5: When fuel reaches the required reserve
column6: When the boost pump inlet first uncovers
column7: Under 14 CFR 25.1337, zero corresponds to the established unusable fuel quantity for that tank in level flight.

column2: Which change does jettisoning fuel achieve for a transport returning soon after a heavy takeoff?
column4: Shift fuel to restore lateral balance
column5: Feed the engines from a common supply
column7: Jettison removes fuel from the aircraft, reducing total weight while retaining the fuel required for flight. Moving fuel between tanks changes distribution.

column2: The right engine is drawing directly from the left wing tank. Which multiengine fuel arrangement allows this?
column7: A crossfeed path lets an engine draw from the other side. Transferring fuel to another tank changes where it is stored.

column2: What does LL identify in the designation 100LL avgas?
column7: LL identifies the low-lead version. The FAA handbook distinguishes lead content from the fuel's grade designation.

column2: A center-zero ammeter is wired in the battery lead. What does a minus 8 ampere indication mean?
column7: A negative reading shows net discharge. The battery is supplying more current than it receives.

column2: A loadmeter reads 65% on an alternator rated at 80 amperes. What current is the alternator supplying?
column7: A percent loadmeter shows the fraction of generating capacity in use. Multiplying 80 amperes by 0.65 gives 52 amperes.

column2: A drawing specifies a nominal 12-volt battery. Which regulated generator output is typical when charging it?
column7: The charging source needs a higher output voltage than the battery. The voltage difference permits charging current to flow.

column2: Which part of an alternator installation converts the generated AC into DC for the aircraft bus?
column7: The diodes rectify the alternator's AC output for use by DC equipment and the battery.

column2: An aircraft has a DC bus and an instrument that requires AC. What supplies the required conversion?
column7: An inverter converts DC to AC. A transformer changes AC voltage and a rectifier performs the reverse conversion.

column2: Which feature identifies a distribution bus on an aircraft wiring diagram?
column3: Multiple branch feeds share one supply conductor
column4: Several switch positions share one moving contact
column5: Two coils share one magnetic core
column6: Several diodes share a single DC output
column7: A bus bar distributes electrical power to several circuits from a common point. Each branch can have its own protection.

column2: A breaker is marked trip-free. In an overload test, which observation verifies that feature?
column3: Contacts open with the control restrained closed
column4: Contacts reclose as soon as the element cools
column5: Contacts remain open until the input is removed
column6: Contacts open once the control is manually released
column7: A trip-free mechanism can interrupt the circuit independently of the operating control. Holding the control cannot override the trip.

column2: Which characteristic chiefly affects a DC motor switch when its contacts first close?
column7: A DC motor can draw several times its rated current at startup. Switch selection accounts for the current it must make as well as the running load.

column2: A feeder carries 6 amperes and has 0.08 ohm resistance. What voltage drop does it introduce?
column7: Voltage drop is current times resistance. Six amperes multiplied by 0.08 ohm gives 0.48 volt.

column2: Which cable feature limits electromagnetic pickup in a signal lead routed near other circuits?
column7: The metallic shield screens the signal conductor from stray electromagnetic fields. A woven protective jacket can resist wear without providing electrical shielding.

column2: A wiring bundle passes through a cutout in a metal junction box. What protects the insulation at the opening?
column7: A grommet or equivalent edge protection prevents rubbing against the metal. Bundling the wires alone leaves the edge exposed.

column2: Which component controls generator output as engine speed and electrical demand vary?
column7: The regulator controls generator or alternator output to maintain system voltage and the battery's charging conditions.

column2: Small supercooled droplets freeze on impact, trapping air pockets in a rough, opaque deposit. Which ice has formed?
column7: Rapid freezing traps air, giving rime ice its rough, milky appearance. Slowly freezing water can produce denser, clearer ice.

column2: Which aerodynamic change can leading-edge ice cause compared with the clean wing?
column3: Lower maximum lift and earlier stall
column4: Higher maximum lift and earlier stall
column5: Lower maximum lift and later stall
column6: Higher maximum lift and later stall
column7: Ice changes airflow over the leading edge. The wing can reach its reduced maximum lift at a smaller angle of attack.

column2: A vibrating detector accumulates ice. Which signal tells its electronics that the probe mass has changed?
column7: Accreted ice adds mass to the vibrating element and changes its frequency. The electronics use that change to identify accretion.

column2: Between cycles, a pneumatic boot stays tight against the wing. What condition exists inside its tubes?
column5: Pressure at the full inflation setting
column6: Pressure above ambient but below the inflation setting
column7: Vacuum collapses the tubes against the surface between cycles, preserving the normal airfoil contour.

column2: A sectioned wing shows small holes in a piccolo tube aimed at the leading-edge skin. What flows through it?
column7: The perforations direct hot air onto the inside of the leading-edge skin. Heating the skin helps prevent ice from forming on its exterior.

column2: Four propeller blades are numbered in order around the hub. Which section pairs with blade 1's outer section for balanced deicing?
column7: Heaters operate on corresponding sections of opposite blades to limit imbalance as ice sheds. With four blades, blade 3 is opposite blade 1.

column2: Which observation distinguishes runback from ice left behind by a completed heating cycle?
column3: Water flows aft and freezes beyond the heated strip
column4: Ice remains attached where the heater just operated
column5: Fresh droplets freeze between successive heat cycles
column6: Ice first appears on an unheated projecting probe
column7: Water travels beyond the heated area and freezes on colder skin. Its movement aft before freezing identifies runback ice.

column2: Which arrangement heats the windshield laminate itself on a typical electrically anti-iced transport?
column3: Conductive film embedded in the pane
column4: Heated panel attached to the outer face
column5: Warm airflow directed across the inner face
column6: Fluid distributed over the exterior surface
column7: A conductive film or fine heating wires carry current within the windshield. Their resistance supplies heat across the viewing area.

column2: Which boot inspection finding provides a direct path for surface moisture to enter during the suction cycle?
column5: Scuffing confined to the surface coating
column6: Crease in the bond line beneath the boot
column7: Moisture can enter through the damaged surface when vacuum is applied. Freezing inside the boot can interfere with its operation.

column2: A windshield rain repellent has just been applied. Which water pattern indicates its intended action in flight?
column4: Continuous film draining down the pane
column5: Clear band traced by the blade sweep
column6: Dry strip directly in front of an air nozzle
column7: Repellent changes how water wets the glass. Airflow removes the resulting beads from the treated surface.

column2: Which means of clearing a windshield uses a pneumatic rain-removal nozzle?
column3: Deflecting drops with an external air curtain
column4: Evaporating droplets on an electrically heated pane
column5: Removing beaded water with the slipstream
column6: Sweeping water aside with a powered blade
column7: Compressor bleed air directed across the windshield forms an air curtain. This diverts incoming drops before they reach the glass.

column2: A wiper reaches both limits on time but leaves streaks at high airspeed. Which quantity can fall under aerodynamic loading?
column3: Blade force normal to the pane
column7: Aerodynamic forces can unload the wiper blade and reduce its pressure against the pane. A blade that no longer bears evenly can leave streaks.
